english.title: Engage with others in prohibited conduct intending an interference effect
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) engaged in a course of conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY COURSE OF CONDUCT..), with one or more other persons, the course of conduct in question, or a course of conduct of which it formed part, being carried out for or on behalf of a foreign power or designated body, when you knew, or having regard to other matters known to you, ought to have known that to be the case, intending the course of conduct to have an interference effect, namely **(..SPECIFY INTERFERENCE EFFECT..), and, as part of the course of conduct, another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) engaged in prohibited conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY PROHIBITED CONDUCT..), when you intended or believed that, as part of the course of conduct, another person would engage in prohibited conduct
english.legislation: Contrary to section 13(3) and (7) of the National Security Act 2023.

english.notes:
(i) This offence applies from 8th July 2026 due to the introduction of the designated body condition by the National Security (State Threats) Act 2026. This offence mirrors the structure of the previous offence but includes a designated body as well as a foreign power. For the offence applying before this date, see H101424.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
(iii) Section 13 makes provision for three offences of foreign interference. There are four concepts that are common to all three offences: interference effects (section 14); prohibited conduct (section 15); the foreign power condition (section 31) or the designated body condition (section 33B) and conduct/courses of conduct. For the offence applicable where an individual engages in prohibited conduct recklessly having an interference effect, see H102844. See H102843 for the offence applicable where an individual intends that effect. This document provides for an offence where a person engages in a course of conduct with one or more persons and one of those other persons engages in prohibited conduct. This ensures that a person can commit a foreign interference offence where the person does not carry out the prohibited conduct themselves, but has others do so.
(iv) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
